short: A minor tactical defeat that shattered the myth of Swedish military invincibility.
full:
Fought on 28 June 1675, the Battle of Fehrbellin occurred when a Swedish army, allied with France, invaded the Margraviate of Brandenburg. Intending to force Elector Frederick William out of the Franco-Dutch War, the Swedish forces found themselves bogged down and cut off during their retreat. A smaller but highly motivated Brandenburg army caught the Swedes near the town of Fehrbellin.

While casualties were relatively low and the battle was tactically indecisive, its strategic and psychological impact was profound. The Brandenburgers successfully routed the previously undefeated Swedish army, destroying the aura of invincibility that had surrounded Swedish forces since the Thirty Years' War. This perceived weakness emboldened Denmark and other regional powers to enter the Scanian War, initiating a multi-front conflict that nearly collapsed the Swedish Empire.
